title: Eutychus raised at Troas + Paul's farewell to the Ephesian elders at Miletus

paragraphs.text: And after the uproar ceased, Paul having sent for the disciples and exhorted them, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι τὸν θόρυβον μεταπεμψάμενος ὁ Παῦλος τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ παρακαλέσας, ἀσπασάμενος ἐξῆλθεν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Μακεδονίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Meta de to pausasthai ton thorybon metapempsamenos ho Paulos tous mathētas kai parakalesas, aspasamenos exēlthen poreuesthai eis Makedonian.

paragraphs.text: And when he had gone through those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece.
paragraphs.original: διελθὼν δὲ τὰ μέρη ἐκεῖνα καὶ παρακαλέσας αὐτοὺς λόγῳ πολλῷ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα
paragraphs.translit: dielthōn de ta merē ekeina kai parakalesas autous logō pollō ēlthen eis tēn Hellada

paragraphs.text: And when he had spent three months [there,] and a plot was laid against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.
paragraphs.original: ποιήσας τε μῆνας τρεῖς· γενομένης ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων μέλλοντι ἀνάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν Συρίαν ἐγένετο γνώμης τοῦ ὑποστρέφειν διὰ Μακεδονίας.
paragraphs.translit: poiēsas te mēnas treis· genomenēs epiboulēs autō hypo tōn Ioudaiōn mellonti anagesthai eis tēn Syrian egeneto gnōmēs tou hypostrephein dia Makedonias.

paragraphs.text: And there accompanied him as far as Asia, Sopater of Beroea, [the son] of Pyrrhus; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
paragraphs.original: συνείπετο δὲ αὐτῷ Σώπατρος Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος, Θεσσαλονικέων δὲ Ἀρίσταρχος καὶ Σεκοῦνδος, καὶ Γάϊος Δερβαῖος καὶ Τιμόθεος, Ἀσιανοὶ δὲ Τυχικὸς καὶ Τρόφιμος·
paragraphs.translit: syneipeto de autō Sōpatros Pyrrou Beroiaios, Thessalonikeōn de Aristarchos kai Sekoundos, kai Gaios Derbaios kai Timotheos, Asianoi de Tychikos kai Trophimos·

paragraphs.text: But these had gone before, and were waiting for us at Troas.
paragraphs.original: οὗτοι δὲ προσελθόντες ἔμενον ἡμᾶς ἐν Τρῳάδι·
paragraphs.translit: houtoi de proselthontes emenon hēmas en Trōadi·

paragraphs.text: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days, where we tarried seven days.
paragraphs.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐξεπλεύσαμεν μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἀζύμων ἀπὸ Φιλίππων, καὶ ἤλθομεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα ἄχρι ἡμερῶν πέντε, οὗ διετρίψαμεν ἡμέρας ἑπτά.
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis de exepleusamen meta tas hēmeras tōn azymōn apo Philippōn, kai ēlthomen pros autous eis tēn Trōada achri hēmerōn pente, hou dietripsamen hēmeras hepta.

paragraphs.text: And upon the first day of the week, when we were gathered together to break bread, Paul discoursed with them, intending to depart on the morrow; and prolonged his speech until midnight.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν δὲ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων συνηγμένων ἡμῶν κλάσαι ἄρτον ὁ Παῦλος διελέγετο αὐτοῖς, μέλλων ἐξιέναι τῇ ἐπαύριον, παρέτεινέν τε τὸν λόγον μέχρι μεσονυκτίου.
paragraphs.translit: En de tē mia tōn sabbatōn synēgmenōn hēmōn klasai arton ho Paulos dielegeto autois, mellōn exienai tē epaurion, pareteinen te ton logon mechri mesonyktiou.

paragraphs.text: And there were many lights in the upper chamber where we were gathered together.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δὲ λαμπάδες ἱκαναὶ ἐν τῷ ὑπερῴῳ οὗ ἦμεν συνηγμένοι·
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de lampades hikanai en tō hyperōō hou ēmen synēgmenoi·

paragraphs.text: And there sat in the window a certain young man named Eutychus, borne down with deep sleep; and as Paul discoursed yet longer, being borne down by his sleep he fell down from the third story, and was taken up dead.
paragraphs.original: καθεζόμενος δέ τις νεανίας ὀνόματι Εὔτυχος ἐπὶ τῆς θυρίδος, καταφερόμενος ὕπνῳ βαθεῖ διαλεγομένου τοῦ Παύλου ἐπὶ πλεῖον, κατενεχθεὶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἔπεσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ τριστέγου κάτω καὶ ἤρθη νεκρός.
paragraphs.translit: kathezomenos de tis neanias onomati Eutychos epi tēs thyridos, katapheromenos hypnō bathei dialegomenou tou Paulou epi pleion, katenechtheis apo tou hypnou epesen apo tou tristegou katō kai ērthē nekros.

paragraphs.text: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Make ye no ado; for his life is in him.
paragraphs.original: καταβὰς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐπέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ συμπεριλαβὼν εἶπεν· Μὴ θορυβεῖσθε, ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: katabas de ho Paulos epepesen autō kai symperilabōn eipen· Mē thorybeisthe, hē gar psychē autou en autō estin.

paragraphs.text: And when he was gone up, and had broken the bread, and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
paragraphs.original: ἀναβὰς δὲ καὶ κλάσας τὸν ἄρτον καὶ γευσάμενος ἐφʼ ἱκανόν τε ὁμιλήσας ἄχρι αὐγῆς, οὕτως ἐξῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: anabas de kai klasas ton arton kai geusamenos ephʼ hikanon te homilēsas achri augēs, houtōs exēlthen.

paragraphs.text: And they brought the lad alive, and were not a little comforted.
paragraphs.original: ἤγαγον δὲ τὸν παῖδα ζῶντα, καὶ παρεκλήθησαν οὐ μετρίως.
paragraphs.translit: ēgagon de ton paida zōnta, kai pareklēthēsan ou metriōs.

paragraphs.text: But we going before to the ship set sail for Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, intending himself to go by land.
paragraphs.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ προελθόντες ἐπὶ τὸ πλοῖον ἀνήχθημεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἆσσον, ἐκεῖθεν μέλλοντες ἀναλαμβάνειν τὸν Παῦλον, οὕτως γὰρ διατεταγμένος ἦν μέλλων αὐτὸς πεζεύειν.
paragraphs.translit: Hēmeis de proelthontes epi to ploion anēchthēmen epi tēn Asson, ekeithen mellontes analambanein ton Paulon, houtōs gar diatetagmenos ēn mellōn autos pezeuein.

paragraphs.text: And when he met us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ συνέβαλλεν ἡμῖν εἰς τὴν Ἆσσον, ἀναλαβόντες αὐτὸν ἤλθομεν εἰς Μιτυλήνην,
paragraphs.translit: hōs de syneballen hēmin eis tēn Asson, analabontes auton ēlthomen eis Mitylēnēn,

paragraphs.text: And sailing from thence, we came the following day over against Chios; and the next day we touched at Samos; and the day after we came to Miletus.
paragraphs.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀποπλεύσαντες τῇ ἐπιούσῃ κατηντήσαμεν ἄντικρυς Χίου, τῇ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ παρεβάλομεν εἰς Σάμον, τῇ δὲ ἐχομένῃ ἤλθομεν εἰς Μίλητον·
paragraphs.translit: kakeithen apopleusantes tē epiousē katēntēsamen antikrys Chiou, tē de hetera parebalomen eis Samon, tē de echomenē ēlthomen eis Milēton·

paragraphs.text: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
paragraphs.original: κεκρίκει γὰρ ὁ Παῦλος παραπλεῦσαι τὴν Ἔφεσον, ὅπως μὴ γένηται αὐτῷ χρονοτριβῆσαι ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ἔσπευδεν γὰρ εἰ δυνατὸν εἴη αὐτῷ τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς γενέσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
paragraphs.translit: kekrikei gar ho Paulos parapleusai tēn Epheson, hopōs mē genētai autō chronotribēsai en tē Asia, espeuden gar ei dynaton eiē autō tēn hēmeran tēs pentēkostēs genesthai eis Hierosolyma.

paragraphs.text: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called to him the elders of the church.
paragraphs.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς Μιλήτου πέμψας εἰς Ἔφεσον μετεκαλέσατο τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
paragraphs.translit: Apo de tēs Milētou pempsas eis Epheson metekalesato tous presbyterous tēs ekklēsias.

paragraphs.text: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, after what manner I was with you all the time,
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ παρεγένοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ἀπὸ πρώτης ἡμέρας ἀφʼ ἧς ἐπέβην εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν πῶς μεθʼ ὑμῶν τὸν πάντα χρόνον ἐγενόμην,
paragraphs.translit: hōs de paregenonto pros auton eipen autois· Hymeis epistasthe apo prōtēs hēmeras aphʼ hēs epebēn eis tēn Asian pōs methʼ hymōn ton panta chronon egenomēn,

paragraphs.text: serving the Lord with all lowliness of mind, and with tears, and with trials which befell me by the plots of the Jews;
paragraphs.original: δουλεύων τῷ κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ δακρύων καὶ πειρασμῶν τῶν συμβάντων μοι ἐν ταῖς ἐπιβουλαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων·
paragraphs.translit: douleuōn tō kyriō meta pasēs tapeinophrosynēs kai dakryōn kai peirasmōn tōn symbantōn moi en tais epiboulais tōn Ioudaiōn·

paragraphs.text: how I shrank not from declaring unto you anything that was profitable, and teaching you publicly, and from house to house,
paragraphs.original: ὡς οὐδὲν ὑπεστειλάμην τῶν συμφερόντων τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ὑμῖν καὶ διδάξαι ὑμᾶς δημοσίᾳ καὶ κατʼ οἴκους,
paragraphs.translit: hōs ouden hypesteilamēn tōn sympherontōn tou mē anangeilai hymin kai didaxai hymas dēmosia kai katʼ oikous,

paragraphs.text: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
paragraphs.original: διαμαρτυρόμενος Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τὴν εἰς θεὸν μετάνοιαν καὶ πίστιν εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: diamartyromenos Ioudaiois te kai Hellēsin tēn eis theon metanoian kai pistin eis ton kyrion hēmōn Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
paragraphs.original: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ δεδεμένος ἐγὼ τῷ πνεύματι πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ συναντήσοντά μοι μὴ εἰδώς,
paragraphs.translit: kai nyn idou dedemenos egō tō pneumati poreuomai eis Ierousalēm, ta en autē synantēsonta moi mē eidōs,

paragraphs.text: save that the Holy Spirit testifieth unto me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν ὅτι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί μοι λέγον ὅτι δεσμὰ καὶ θλίψεις με μένουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: plēn hoti to pneuma to hagion kata polin diamartyretai moi legon hoti desma kai thlipseis me menousin·

paragraphs.text: But I hold not my life of any account as dear unto myself, so that I may accomplish my course, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ οὐδενὸς λόγου ποιοῦμαι τὴν ψυχὴν τιμίαν ἐμαυτῷ ὡς τελειῶσαι τὸν δρόμον μου καὶ τὴν διακονίαν ἣν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, διαμαρτύρασθαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ oudenos logou poioumai tēn psychēn timian emautō hōs teleiōsai ton dromon mou kai tēn diakonian hēn elabon para tou kyriou Iēsou, diamartyrasthai to euangelion tēs charitos tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I went about preaching the kingdom, shall see my face no more.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι οὐκέτι ὄψεσθε τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὑμεῖς πάντες ἐν οἷς διῆλθον κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai nyn idou egō oida hoti ouketi opsesthe to prosōpon mou hymeis pantes en hois diēlthon kēryssōn tēn basileian.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore I testify unto you this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
paragraphs.original: διότι μαρτύρομαι ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σήμερον ἡμέρᾳ ὅτι καθαρός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος πάντων,
paragraphs.translit: dioti martyromai hymin en tē sēmeron hēmera hoti katharos eimi apo tou haimatos pantōn,

paragraphs.text: For I shrank not from declaring unto you the whole counsel of God.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ὑπεστειλάμην τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι πᾶσαν τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar hypesteilamēn tou mē anangeilai pasan tēn boulēn tou theou hymin.

paragraphs.text: Take heed unto yourselves, and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit hath made you bishops, to feed the church of the Lord which he purchased with his own blood.
paragraphs.original: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ, ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπους, ποιμαίνειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἣν περιεποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου.
paragraphs.translit: prosechete heautois kai panti tō poimniō, en hō hymas to pneuma to hagion etheto episkopous, poimainein tēn ekklēsian tou theou, hēn periepoiēsato dia tou haimatos tou idiou.

paragraphs.text: I know that after my departing grievous wolves shall enter in among you, not sparing the flock;
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι εἰσελεύσονται μετὰ τὴν ἄφιξίν μου λύκοι βαρεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς μὴ φειδόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου,
paragraphs.translit: egō oida hoti eiseleusontai meta tēn aphixin mou lykoi bareis eis hymas mē pheidomenoi tou poimniou,

paragraphs.text: and from among your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα τοῦ ἀποσπᾶν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω ἑαυτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: kai ex hymōn autōn anastēsontai andres lalountes diestrammena tou apospan tous mathētas opisō heautōn·

paragraphs.text: Wherefore watch ye, remembering that by the space of three years I ceased not to admonish every one night and day with tears.
paragraphs.original: διὸ γρηγορεῖτε, μνημονεύοντες ὅτι τριετίαν νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν οὐκ ἐπαυσάμην μετὰ δακρύων νουθετῶν ἕνα ἕκαστον.
paragraphs.translit: dio grēgoreite, mnēmoneuontes hoti trietian nykta kai hēmeran ouk epausamēn meta dakryōn nouthetōn hena hekaston.

paragraphs.text: And now I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build [you] up, and to give [you] the inheritance among all them that are sanctified.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν παρατίθεμαι ὑμᾶς τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, τῷ δυναμένῳ οἰκοδομῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν κληρονομίαν ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πᾶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ta nyn paratithemai hymas tō theō kai tō logō tēs charitos autou, tō dynamenō oikodomēsai kai dounai tēn klēronomian en tois hēgiasmenois pasin.

paragraphs.text: I coveted no man`s silver, or gold, or apparel.
paragraphs.original: ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα·
paragraphs.translit: argyriou ē chrysiou ē himatismou oudenos epethymēsa·

paragraphs.text: Ye yourselves know that these hands ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
paragraphs.original: αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσι μετʼ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται.
paragraphs.translit: autoi ginōskete hoti tais chreiais mou kai tois ousi metʼ emou hypēretēsan hai cheires hautai.

paragraphs.text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring ye ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
paragraphs.original: πάντα ὑπέδειξα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως κοπιῶντας δεῖ ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τῶν ἀσθενούντων, μνημονεύειν τε τῶν λόγων τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπεν Μακάριόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον διδόναι ἢ λαμβάνειν.
paragraphs.translit: panta hypedeixa hymin hoti houtōs kopiōntas dei antilambanesthai tōn asthenountōn, mnēmoneuein te tōn logōn tou kyriou Iēsou hoti autos eipen Makarion estin mallon didonai ē lambanein.

paragraphs.text: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down and prayed with them all.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν θεὶς τὰ γόνατα αὐτοῦ σὺν πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς προσηύξατο.
paragraphs.translit: Kai tauta eipōn theis ta gonata autou syn pasin autois prosēuxato.

paragraphs.text: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul`s neck and kissed him,
paragraphs.original: ἱκανὸς δὲ κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο πάντων, καὶ ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Παύλου κατεφίλουν αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: hikanos de klauthmos egeneto pantōn, kai epipesontes epi ton trachēlon tou Paulou katephiloun auton,

paragraphs.text: sorrowing most of all for the word which he had spoken, that they should behold his face no more. And they brought him on his way unto the ship.
paragraphs.original: ὀδυνώμενοι μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ᾧ εἰρήκει ὅτι οὐκέτι μέλλουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ θεωρεῖν. προέπεμπον δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον.
paragraphs.translit: odynōmenoi malista epi tō logō hō eirēkei hoti ouketi mellousin to prosōpon autou theōrein. proepempon de auton eis to ploion.
